newsitem.title: USA: Mail cars plunge into water as mudslide hits train.
newsitem.headline: Mail cars plunge into water as mudslide hits train.

text.p: A Burlington Northern Santa Fe Corp. freight train was derailed by a mudslide, sending five cars carrying bulk mail and other cargo into the chilly waters of Puget Sound, authorities said Thursday.

Coast Guard Lt. Russ Read said the southbound train derailed shortly before 11 p.m. Wednesday about 14 miles north of Seattle after a slide swept down and buried nearly 100 yards of track under 25 feet of mud and debris.
The slide slammed into the 35-car freight train just behind its three locomotives, sending five cars into the Sound, said railroad spokesman Gus Melonas. No one was injured.
Ernie Swanson, a spokesman for the Seattle district office of the U.S. Postal Service, said the train carried 11 trailer-sized containers of bulk mail, six of which were lost in the accident.

Swanson did not know how many pieces of mail were involved but said it was a mix of catalogues, advertising mailers, periodicals and packages headed for the Seattle sorting facility from five bulk mail centres in the East.
"You're talking thousands and thousands and thousands of pieces, no doubt," he said.
A second mud slide in the same area Thursday morning forced the evacuation of about 15 people who lived in a convent and nearby house.

Melonas said freight traffic to the Seattle area was being rerouted onto two more southerly routes, and the railroad hoped to reopen the track within 48 hours. The slide also has disrupted Amtrak passenger train service between Seattle and Vancouver, B.C.
Once the mail is fished out of the water, postal officials will bring it to the regional handling centre to see if it can be salvaged, Swanson said.
"If it's just water damage and it looks like it still has value we'll try to dry it out and eventually get it delivered," he said. "If it's not deliverable we'll just chalk it up to waste."
